![](/dns/root-servers-map){fig-alt="map of DNS root servers, indicating that there are hundreds in eastern North America, tens in the pacific northwest, hundreds in Europe, hundreds in the middle east, tens in east asia, hundreds in southeast asia, hundreds in Africa, tens in oceania, and even one K in Greenland, a couple in Hawaii and Alaska, etc."}


### anycast root servers  {.smaller}


* many root servers have multiple separate sites
* … but one IPv4/IPv6 address 
<hr class="vspace" />
* which one you get = which one routed to
* multiple sites with BGP announcements for IP 
   * often with care taken to limit how far route goes
* idea called ‘anycast’ 
   * get to ‘any’ of several servers
* also used for some public recursive DNS servers 
   * 1.1.1.1 (CloudFlare), 8.8.8.8 (Google), 208.67.222.222 (Cisco), …
